request.instruction: Write the final wording of these three fictional knowledge-work task templates in your own clear words. Preserve every rule, all exact field names, inclusive bounds, tie breaks and the {SPECIFICATIONS}/{COMPANY} placeholders. Do not solve, change, weaken or add a rule. Output ONLY a JSON object with keys calendar, finqa, repl, each a string. No tools. These tasks will be tested on OpenAI models.

templates.calendar: You are Alice, managing cal-alice, cal-bob and cal-carol as availability copies. Reschedule the three existing Project review A/B/C appointments as one planning bundle on 4 November 2026. Find their event IDs through the API. Keep each identity, title, calendar, duration and attendees. Do not create or delete any events. Read all three calendars before the first write. Returned times are UTC. Protected appointments must stay unchanged. When checking proposed availability, ignore all three old Project review appointments because all three will move; every other event is busy. Each review must fit every listed person's calendar. Reviews cannot overlap, and A must end at least 15 minutes before C starts. Use only the listed start options. Minimize the sum over reviews of weight * absolute(start minus original start in minutes). Break a tie by earliest A start, then earliest B, then earliest C. Patch the three existing events to the unique selected times, then finish. No Python tool is supplied in this environment. Appointment specifications: {SPECIFICATIONS}
templates.finqa: Company {COMPANY} has a single heterogeneous ledger table; all record types are in ledger so SQL self-joins and CTEs are possible. Close the payable ledger as known at recorded_at <= 2026-10-24T12:00:00, for business_date <= 2026-10-23. All timestamps are UTC ISO text. First exclude future business dates and late recorded rows, then keep the highest revision for each (kind,event_key). A latest row with status void removes that key; never resurrect an older row. Invoice rows use event_key as invoice ID; payment, credit and hold rows use invoice_id as their parent. Keep active invoices for vendor BLUE, due_date <= 2026-10-30. Payments and credits reduce gross amount_minor, in the invoice currency. Active holds reduce the remaining amount; release/void holds do not. Clamp remaining=max(0,gross-sum(payments)-sum(credits)), then unheld=max(0,remaining-sum(active holds)). For each invoice choose the active terms row with the same terms_code and greatest business_date <= the invoice business_date (after the same revision/as-of filtering). Discount is unheld * (10000-discount_bps)/10000 only when 2026-10-23 <= discount_until, otherwise unheld. Then select the active FX row of that invoice currency with greatest business_date <= invoice business_date. Convert with fx_num/fx_den to USD cents. Round only this final invoice amount to the nearest cent, with exact halves rounded up. Sum rounded invoice USD cents. Invoices in USD also have FX rows. Do not net invoices together before rounding. Submit just the integer USD cents.
templates.repl: The complete JSON procurement workbook is in the Python variable context. Load it using json.loads(context). Select exactly one quote for each of the five SKUs A-E. Quotes are indivisible lots. Each quote must supply at least the SKU demand and at most demand+2 units, arrive on or before that SKU deadline, and have quality approved. Across selected quotes use at least three vendors, total carbon <= carbon_cap, and for each vendor total selected units <= unit_cap. A quote with needs_same_vendor_sku must have the selected quote for that other SKU from the same vendor. For each vendor compute gross=sum(units*unit_cents). If selected units >= tier_units, apply its tier_bps discount to the entire gross; round that vendor merchandise total to cents, exact halves up. Add shipping_cents unless PRE-DISCOUNT gross >= free_shipping_gross. Subtract rebate_cents only if at least two different SKUs are selected from that vendor AND the POST-DISCOUNT merchandise total >= rebate_merchandise_min. All thresholds are inclusive. Total cost is the sum across used vendors. Find the globally minimum total cost in cents, not a greedy per-SKU choice. Return only that integer using print(FINAL(str(answer))) or submit_answer. All values and rules are fictional for this experiment. No orders will be placed.
